 Elizabeth Holmes Look-Alike Contest Draws Mass of Black Turtlenecks to Lafayette Park
 By Zack Ruskin 
 • 
 November 8, 2026 · 1:09 PM PST 
 • 
 2 min read 
 Photo @threegirlsinsf /Instagram 
 X 
 Facebook 
 Copy link 
 Saturday saw a horde of Elizabeth Holmes converge on San Francisco's Lafayette Park alongside a few hundred spectators for a look-alike contest inspired by A24's new meta-documentary mega hit You Can See Everything . A plastic surgery resident at Stanford University took home top honors.
 As the Chronicle reports , approximately two dozen would-be Elizabeth Holmes turned out to do battle in a contest organized by a handful of 20-something SF residents. 
 Inspired by the turnout at a New York edition that took place in last month , organizers say a Partiful listing for the look-alike contest received 1,000 RSVPS almost as soon as it went live.
 @threegirlsinsf /Instagram The event also saw a contest held for the best Nathan Fielder look-alike, ensuring You Can See Everything 's on-screen co-director wasn't missing from the afternoon's festivities.
 Incredibly, organizers managed to secure an impressively fitting sponsor for the whole affair: Think Jerky, the Texas jerky brand who makes a memorable cameo late in the film once Holmes has reported to prison.
 “The jerky is everything,” attendee Kristyn Braden told the Chronicle.
 View this post on Instagram A post shared by ALEX (@a.little.extra.alex) 
 Ultimately, Stanford University plastic surgery resident Sierra Stingl was selected as the contestant who most closely resembled the disgraced Theranos founder. Amazingly, per the Chronicle, the 30-year-old Stingl has also received funding from Stanford to develop a medical device.
 “It’s a little eerie, given my background,” Stingl told the Chronicle of her victory.
 In remarks captured by KRON4 , organizer and co-host Tanvi Kaur celebrated the event for being the good kind of weird.
 “Historically, SF has been a place for weird people, creative energy, and a lot of really cool ideas," Kaur said. "I feel like we are losing a little bit of that spark, so our whole mission is to bring that fun and audacity back to the city. I think we need more audacity."
